meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in, so did you ask him that before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Is anything on his record right now, and who else has seen that screen?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A seventeen-year-old misplaces a quotation, so is it anywhere else in the play? And you didn't answer me. Is anything on his record right now?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. Twice now you've stepped past his record, so I'll stop asking: nothing goes in his file, and none of this goes near his class. What is it you want from him?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
An outline is a plan, and people change their minds in two weeks. That's the third thing you've shown me and you still haven't said what you want from him, Hale.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. He'll sit it, to put this behind him and for no other reason. Private, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all of it in my inbox tonight under 4.4.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. He'll be there. What time, and who else is in the room?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

cc: Principal

Hale,

You agreed that Owen will sit a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday the twelfth after school, not in front of his class, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require the time, who else will be in the room, who else has seen what you showed me, whether Owen was heard before the zero was entered, and whether anything is on his record right now. You said I would have this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, confirmed in writing tonight. She still wants the time, who will be in the room, who else has seen your evidence, whether Owen was heard before the zero, and whether anything is on his record now. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times right after owning the zero in one sentence. It was dated, it was Owen's own document, and she could check it herself.
What cost ground: You skipped her question about his record twice and showed more evidence instead. That is the thing she fears most, so each skip made her sharper.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop. Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay in three edits between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October, which is as close as evidence gets to that night. It proves nothing about the essay. It is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asks whether anything is on his record right now, answer in one sentence before you open the play, because the answer was no and it would have cost you nothing.
